design.pending_check: The check waits at most CheckLockWait = 10 s for the ledger lock. On failure it writes a coalesced <db>.check-pending.json (first/last time, count, last reason, pid) under its own <db>.checker.lock, atomically (tmp+rename), without the ledger lock, and exits nonzero ('check incomplete'). It never reports a completed check. The pending ledger work is retried automatically: by run after every pass (EscalateTimeouts), by every ledger holder (the ProcessDue ack drain), and, with run stopped, by the next check on the 30 s timer. Nothing clears the marker except a check that completes (ReconcileCheck); nothing recurses into the lock from the handler.
design.owner: OnFailure handler 'agent-loop checker-failed': no ledger lock, no dependence on run or the check. It reads the failed unit's Result/ExecMainCode/ExecMainStatus (2 s) and keeps one incident: dedup across failures; the record is written before any send; duty is told at once (wake 5 s, rc 0/3 only); the director when duty's wake fails, or when the incident still fails 60 s after duty was told. The incident closes only on a completed check, which tells duty RECOVERED once.
design.bounds: One check: systemctl 2 s + alarms 2 x 2.5 s + lock wait 10 s + hold 10.5 s + read 1 s = 28.5 s < TimeoutStartSec 35 s. Handler: 2 + 5 + 5 = 12 s < 20 s. Refusal or held lock -> duty told within 10 s wait + about 0.6 s handler after the check starts (measured 10.1 s). Hang -> killed at 35 s, owner at once (measured 35.1 s). Kill -> owner at once (measured 2.0 s, killed at 2 s).
design.host_boundary: Not covered: the calendar timer not firing, and the systemd user manager being down (both stop the check and its handler). Not claimed, not tested.
